Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Design & Drill All Aboard Train, 30 Piece Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark and the DJI Tello, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for 35 dollars. Compared to other drones, I would say that there are certain improvements that could be made but those drones are much, much more expensive.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is quite small, which is nice because it lends itself to indoor flight and easy travel. It is about 4.5 inches by 4.5 inches for a length and width, and the diagonal rotor distance is about 5 inches, while to entire copter stands at about 1.25 inches. This, as I said, is nice for indoor flight and you don't have to worry too much about hitting someone. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards proved themselves quite useful, as I bumped it into walls several times, and the guards did their job. The copter simply bounced off the wall and continued flying. Additionally, when I was testing it, the drone died while flying. I knew this was coming, as I could feel the responsiveness beginning to slow and the flip function would no longer work. The drone fell from about 12 feet in the air onto the blacktop. I didn't notice and dings, dents, or scar=tches, and once it was charged, it flew fine.

Quiet - The drone has a shrill high pitched sound as it flies. It isn't too loud, and I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. Executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward of backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button a the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Cons:
Disproportionate flight to charge time ratio - According to the user manual, this charge time is about 70 minutes, while the flight time is around 5 minutes while hovering. I, however, found that it took about 35 minutes (charging for a wall outlet) for a full charge from dropping out of the sky dead. The flight time that I got was about 6 minutes, doing maneuvers, flips, climbing, falling, accelerating and decelerating. Still, I think this could be improved, and, as there are no removable batteries you can plug in once another is dead, I make using the drone for more than 10 minutes hard.
Poor wind resistance - This thing blows outside with the slightest breeze. Inside, the flight trim is hard to adjust, and outside, it is not worth it. I found myself constantly adjusting to compensate for any wind.
Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as find things within the manual. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
Joysticks don't articulate much - This is actually somewhat annoying. there isn't much height to the sticks, and they don't move around much, making any more precise movements difficult. Additionally, the other buttons on the controller are somewhat difficult to press.

I liked this drone, especially for the price. This would be great for any kid, or even as a starting copter for someone who wants to see if they are interested in them. I like the size, durability, and flip function, but the battery life and wind resistance are something to consider.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls

LEGO Classic Bricks and Houses 11008 Kids’ Building Toy Starter Set with Fun Builds to Stimulate Young Minds (270 Pieces) The Lego Classic Bricks and Houses set is more open ended than themed sets. The included instructions give steps for a small house, a castle, an igloo, a windmill, a family home, and a lighthouse. You can build all of these at the same time, without having to deconstruct anything.

This set reminded me of when I was a kid, taking out my bucket of Legos and just building whatever came to mind, instead of following the instructions to a specific set.

This set includes a good assortment of colors and pieces, and hopefully the different building techniques and different house styles will inspire kids to try out their own house, or whatever else they want to build. That’s the aim of the Lego Classic line, to inspire kids to make their own creations, and I think the pieces here are good for that.

It could make a good gift for the beginning Lego builder, especially if you’re unsure of what theme they might prefer, or be a good complement to other Lego Classic sets.

text_fidelity_a:
HOT WHEELS IRON MAN REPULSOR BLAST LAUNCHER Kid enjoys it, but it's not the thrilling launch you were expecting.
The packaging on this Iron Man Hotwheels launcher is eye-catching - the type of thing your child would be immediately drawn to. My 4.5 yo has been pining for this item ever since he caught a glimpse. The toy was easy to remove from the packaging, something we can all rejoice over. The instructions are straightforward, but it was unclear to me if the toy needs to "click in" to be launched or if it is simply placed on the track inside the larger car (the launcher). The mask doesn't close all the way if you click it in, which tells me it's not really meant to be there. I was expecting more of a spring action launch, but it's really just a result of the handle shooting it forward. The results are hit and miss.

As an adult, I found the movement needed to pull back the mask for loading to be slightly awkward (it's a slight lifting motion on a very small tab). My 4.5 yo managed to do it no problem: smaller fingers I suppose. I also found the launching slightly difficult as you need to hold onto the larger vehicle with one hand while pulling back and releasing the handle with enough force to *actually* launch the car. My child thinks any amount of launching is thrilling and doesn't seem to mind that the car sometimes barely leaves the launcher, so I suppose it's fine.

The larger car does have fittings to connect with a track, so that may be helpful (we don't own any HotWheels tracks).

All-in-all, your little Iron Man fan will likely be delighted by this. The adults in your house may not be.
text_fidelity_b: HOT WHEELS IRON MAN REPULSOR BLAST LAUNCHER

text_fidelity_a:
Lost Cities - The Board Game Lost Cities TBG is a lot like the original Lost Cities Card Game, but it supports more than 2-players. That's a nice feature.

For those who don't know, Lost Cities the Card Game is considered legendary among hobby board gamers because it's simple, but deep, meaning that anyone can pick up the rules to the game quite quickly, but there's interesting decision-making and complex outcomes to worry about based on your decisions. Of course, it's only a 2-player game, which can be a downfall for many.

The Board Game version is similar in terms of gameplay. If you've already experienced the card game, I could teach you this version in about 30 seconds. Unfortunately, you'll soon want to be back playing the card game. This game lacks a certain something to make it really fun. It works, and it's still easy to learn and play, but I don't think I'll come back to it all that often unless I'm playing with my daughter. For those who are into more complex games, this one just feels...old fashioned. In all the ways that the card game has aged well, this one hasn't.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is a fun toy that encourages creativity and keeps kids occupied. This stamp kit comes complete with nine different stamps, a small ink pad with pink and purple ink, and five colored pencils for your child's creative enjoyment.

Melissa and Doug toys are known for education, creativity, and durability and most every product the company makes can be counted on to posses at least two of these qualities. The same is true with this toy. The Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set isn't big on educational quality, but it does encourage creativity and the set and storage container are made from wood, for better durability. The wooden container offers easy storage so that pieces do not get lost and the product's individual pieces are designed to last.

Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is simple yet fun and requires little supervision or explaining. My little princesses like this toy and still find it fun, but I have noticed that it lacks the staying power of some of their favorite toys. Unless I suggest it, they are not likely to use it. They do like it, but I think they have become a little bored with it. They prefer toys with movement and sound, and this offers neither.

This stamp set is certainly durable, but one thing that isn't made to last is the ink pad. I like that the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set comes complete with its own ink and my girls strongly appreciate that the ink is colored purple and pink. However, don't expect the ink to last very long. The small blotches of ink will not offer many stamping adventures, so be prepared to purchase additional ink stamps within a few months.

Although not the perfect toy, the Melissa and Doug Princess Wooden Stamp Set is nonetheless a good toy for little princesses everywhere. It has many positive qualities, encourages creativity, and is priced right. Like I said, it lacks staying power, but it has enough positive qualities to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Wooden Stamp Set: Vehicles - 10 Stamps, 5 Colored Pencils, 2-Color Stamp Pad

I settled on this one because it's not pink and the dimensions seemed to be appropriate.

Pros:
If you have a tall two year old, this is the kitchen for you. My son is in the 95% for height. I am 5'10" and everyone else in my family is tall, so you have an idea of how tall he is. It will be at least a year before the counter is at a counter height that adults would expect a counter to be. Currently, it stands at his bottom of his breast bone. He's currently about 36* tall.

Once you put it together, it's sturdy and it comes lots of extra screws and parts just in case, which I needed.

The pot holder and the spatula and spoon you see in the picture also come with it.

The instructions were no more difficult that an Ikea set of a directions.

The hours of playtime during the Christmas break and the look on his face and level of excitement was priceless.

Cons:

You will need two sized Phillips head screwdrivers, a wrench or a set of pliers, and at least FOUR hours to put this together. So, slow down on the egg nog.

It's made of particle board and the overlay is paper not painted so it chips off easily.

It's HEAVY! Over 70 pounds!

OFF GASSING! This is the biggest downfall, which I should have known, but just didn't think of. This product offgasses something terrible! Because the box is extremely heavy and because it was delivered to my front door I just couldn't get this down to the basement or to the garage. (I live in an older, well-established neighborhood where most of the houses are pre-1950, so if your house has a garage in the front of the house unlike mine, which is down a driveway and to the back, try to get the UPS man to take it there!) I could only open the box in the house on Christmas Eve, and thus, the offgassing of the kitchen was really terrible and made me nauseous. I would highly recommend airing it out for at least a week in your garage before you put it together and bring it into your house.

Therefore, the toxic chemicals we no doubt inhaled because of my inability to air this product out is a big reason why this only a three not a four star rating.

Overall, I'm satisfied because my son is happy and loves it. If I had the money or space, I would have just purchased the Pottery Barn kitchen set or if I had the time, I would have just made one inspired from Pinterest, but it was a good $150.00 spent, and I'm sure we'll have it for a long time.

The details on the carriage are nice. There are lots of textures to make it more realistic.  The unicorn is a sturdier plastic piece. The doll has the rigid, no bend legs. Her skirt is a cute, candy print fabric, but the material itself is stiff and doesn't flow or move. In fact, I don't like the skirt at all. Overall, it's an attractive looking set, but the quality is disappointing. With all that said, I think young Barbie fans would probably still enjoy it.

Hot Wheels Track Set with 1:64 Scale Toy Firetruck, City Fire Station with Dragon Nemesis and Track Play, Dragon Drive Firefight We've owned plenty of hotwheels sets, some pretty standard and some pretty creative. This is one of those interesting ones I couldn't really understand until we got it. The car is sort of on an "assisted loop", in that there are points that require your intervention to continue. It starts off being "spit out" by the dragon, then fired from a booth, then launched up a loop, and- if everything goes according to plan - it lands on the head of the dragon which will either fall forward or to the side (not knowing which way is part of the fun). However, if you don't have everything 100% seated properly, it just fails miserably. My kids had trouble getting it to work until I came and reseated some parts more forcefully, but even then we still had a few misfires that caused it not to work.
But I suppose that's the tradeoff of the more obscure track sets, sometimes they are more difficult to operate successfully. Part of the fun is making it work, I think. But if you have a kid who isn't up for that challenge, maybe this isn't the set for them. We actually really liked it, and the payoff when it DOES work is the sort of moment that gets high fives and cheers all around.

American Sign Language Flash Cards - 56 ASL Flash Cards for Kids, Babies, Toddlers. Sign Language for Kids Includes Alphabet, Numbers, Days, & Months. ASL Cards with Pictures and Descriptions. This is the “starter pack”. . . .So you know that there’s more to it. . . There are 56 cards in this pack/set. The cards are coated, which are nice.

These cards are for hearing kids to learn American Sign Language (ASL) and not really for deaf kids. I say that because there are notes / hints / ideas on the back of most cards. That’s nice, but you’re not really going to be able to explain that to a deaf child. These cards might be quite helpful for a hearing child / teen to learn ASL where there's a deaf child in the family.

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, Silly Wheelie Mickey When I first saw this in the flesh, I must say I was impressed (and a little jealous).  It's bigger, heavier (in a good way), and more robust than what I imagined, and it seems really well built.  The toy is ready to go (batteries included) and seems built for real world use.  It works best on hard floors (laminate and wood especially), and the little rubber tracks in the rear wheel (which doesn't rotate as wheels do) do a good job of moving the bike, popping wheelies, and avoiding picking up too much of the hair and debris my St Bernard leaves in his wake.  Speaking of which, the big dog and cats love it too.  The toy moves better than you'd think, and it's every bit as durable as you'd like.  It does get stuck along the wall or fall over, but it keeps going.  Carpet doesn't work nearly as well as harder surfaces.  I wouldn't recommend it for carpet (unless the dense hard stuff). The bright colors and ever present Mickey marketing seem to help keep the kids going as well.  As noted in another review, this isn't really interactive or educational, but it's a fine toy.

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Still, I don't think adults will have that problem, and they really are pretty cool!

Targets:

These are a little smaller than I prefer, but they do come in slightly different sizes and shapes. You get different points for different areas. The darts DO stick really well to these targets, and ONLY these targets, but if the dart hits wrong, it still won't stick. I'd say our darts stuck about half the time with the larger guns, and about 3/4th of the time with the farshot blaster. You can peel the back off and it will stick to the wall/door, but as I mentioned above, I just taped it instead. They're a fun way to create a little "battle" zone in one's room, or just simple target practice.

Overall, we've had tons of fun with these guns, and just think they're all pretty awesome.
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

text_fidelity_a: 4M T-Rex Dinosaur DNA Kit, 4945, Multi What kid doesn't like dinosaurs?  This is perfert for your boy or girl who is into dinosaurs.  I suppose it could be considered an educational toy, but probably only marginally so.  Who says educational toys can't be fun too?  This is especially nice for a kid interested in archeology.  Contains a block of plaster that has embedded into it "DNA" stickers and a glow in the dark dinosaur.  After the fun of digging out the dinosaur and stickers with the included digging tools and brush, they are left with a dinosaur model, so even though the digging fun is over after one time (if they do it all at once), there is something to show for it.  There are also two "augmented reality" (AR) play mats that are completed with the DNA stickers that have been "excavated".  The mats when used with a cell phone and an application from the App Store (for Apple phones) or the Google Play Store (for Androids) produces a 3D dinosaur, visible on the phone.  One problem with this is that it might not work with all cell phones.  It is supposed to work with MOST Apple devices (8.0 and above).  On Android phones the only devices tested are Google Nexus Series, Samsung Galaxy S5 and Samsung Galaxy Tab.  I didn't have a cell phone to test this on, but it seems like it still might be fun even if that part doesn't work.  It's just that you might not be able to use the full capability of the kit if your phone doesn't work with the application.  Also if you give this to a child of only 8 (the lower age limit on this), they may not yet have a cell and you may not want them to have one at that age.  Since this contains many small parts, it needs to be kept away from small children, as there is a choking hazard (box says no one under 3).  I would have loved a toy like this when I was a kid.  Just remember to put down a newspaper when they are working on the plaster block in order to collect all the plaster pieces that are chipped off as they excavate.  Pricing of the kit is very reasonable.  Made in China.

text_fidelity_a:
Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up I have mixed feelings about this set because my kids absolutely loved playing with the kinetic sand. Loved it. The bakeshop playset idea was fun, and while the small number of creative tools made it so that my children were asking for their Play-Doh tools to go with it almost immediately, the new texture was so much fun for them that I cannot give this a poor review. I also loved that we had a miniature Barbie Chelsea sandbox with some sandbox toys, and this kinetic sand filled the sandbox perfectly and allowed us to play at making little sandbox molds, scooping the sand, and incorporating the Chelsea doll into play. That set had previously come with the teeny tiny little container of a kinetic sand like material, but having an ample amount was really fun.

However, we discovered the problem with this stuff about 1/2 hour after cleaning up. I walked past the hard floor area where we had cleaned up afterwards, and nearly fell on my butt. I had already, I thought, cleaned up all the pieces of clay on the floor and given one or two areas a quick wipe down with cleaner, so I was puzzled as to why the floor was so slippery. I cleaned the floor there, and walked around and forgot about it for about five more minutes, when I walked by and almost fell on my butt in another spot. Then my husband almost fell. Then my child did fall. I cleaned the floor thoroughly and there were still patches of occasional area that were just ridiculously slippery, and I don't really understand how it withstood numerous attacks with normal household cleaners. But for days we were discovering slippery areas on our floor that made it really not safe.

So I would give the caveat that if you are going to allow your children to play with kinetic sand, do so outside so that you do not end up with a dangerous situation on your own hard floors.
text_fidelity_b: Kinetic Sand, Bake Shoppe Playset with 1lb of Kinetic Sand and 16 Tools and Molds, for Ages 3 and up
